title: qa(scenarios): refusalMeets never sees a hook's declared refusal; the MCP door serves it as declaredCode beside the status's catalogue code
body:
domain:skills#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb

Filing gate: ① (found while reviewing in-flight work). Contract review 6885289276 of PR #33488 (card #33257, a hook's declared refusal) found this outside its diff. The PR's dev probed the live answer.

## What is wrong

`refusalMeets` in `packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-operation-grade.ts` lets a declared `VALIDATION_FAILED` be met by "the app's own rule": a 4xx answer whose `code` is not in the spec's `ErrorCode` catalogue. Its docblock says a hook's declared refusal (`OVER_RECEIPT` at 422, `ASSET_NOT_IN_STOCK` at 409) "reaches the MCP door with its own code".

On main it does not. The MCP data tools serve a hook's declared refusal with `code` set to the status's catalogue code (for example `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` at 409) and the hook's own code as `declaredCode` (#31407, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`). The runner (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/observe.ts`) keeps `code` and `status` but not `declaredCode`. So `refusalMeets` sees a catalogue code and returns false. No declared hook refusal, at any status, meets `VALIDATION_FAILED` on a live run. The grader's unit tests miss this because they pass `ASSET_NOT_IN_STOCK` in as `code` directly.

Live probe (PR #33488's dev, on main): a sandboxed hook declaring `ASSET_NOT_IN_STOCK` at 409 answers `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with `declaredCode: ASSET_NOT_IN_STOCK`.

## Fix

The runner keeps `declaredCode` on a refused answer. `refusalMeets` treats a present `declaredCode` at a 4xx status as the app's own rule. Re-pin the unit tests on the wire shape the door actually serves. Correct the docblock and `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` to match.

## Reach

The scenario lane's grade of every card whose build refuses through a hook's declared refusal. Skills now teach declared refusals (PR #33488), so builds will hit this more often.
